lighting_state: Lighting and state: production fixtures as authored, campaign clock 1928-11-10 20:00 (Saturday) frozen for the run, the player's service lamp on, carried set and HUD hidden, cinematic launch mode, shop simulation and residents at their 20:00 routine positions. Every frame is a teleported inspection station, not a played route: a clear station proves no access, lock or route.

method.capture: Per semantic space: overview from the clear station farthest from the room centre, reverse view from the clear station farthest from the overview, threshold view from 1.0 m outside the principal door or opening (the leaf is opened by the ordinary door interaction where it is not locked, then closed again), and up to three detail views toward authored anchors, runtime props, windows or doors. City stations reuse OrisonV2CitySweep's shop, bar, floor-survey and street logic and add bodega, alley, facade and subway views.
method.review: Each sheet was read for construction, attachment, use, age, maintenance and consequence (Accord 14), then for whether the resident is legible from the threshold (lived-in acceptance), then against the Bible's Rule of Signal and the period. Observed problems are kept separate from interpretations.
method.limits: Detail targets were chosen automatically; in a few rooms the runtime census assigned a lower floor's ceiling fixture to the floor above, so a detail caption names a flush dome from another level while the frame shows bare wall or ceiling (F04 sheets name F03 ids in six stations, F05 sheets name F04 ids in two; noted by the reviewers; corrected in the committed capture scene for later runs). Two shop markers (funeral parlour IN2, luncheonette IN2), the F04 landing overview pair and seven bar zone markers (LOBBY, STAIR, DECK0-2, WC, WC_SINK) face a wall or a door at arm's length, so those zones are recorded only by their other stations. The city sweep did not set weather; the street frames show the scene's default state at the frozen hour (clear sky, dry road), which is evidence of neither the storm nor its absence. Overviews do not accept unseen detail. Small rooms are obstructed by their own fixtures. Night lighting is the canonical state; daylight was not captured. Sealed and restricted interiors were reached by teleport only. No route, lock, save or runtime contract is proved by any image here.

areas.title: The laundry: WORS 1610 came from here
areas.location: 7.8 x 7.7 m west basement room off the public core (B1_LAUNDRY_DOOR); two washers, the airer, tubs
areas.users: every household on its day; Teresa at 03:00 Saturday; Juno and her recorder on Thursdays
areas.narrative: Two galvanised wringer washers, the rinse tubs with their three draped cloths and the rope-and-pulley airer are installed and operate (WasherProp areas, the airer's lower/raise). The room should carry the building's week: a posted laundry schedule (Label3D) by the door with pencil tallies, a basket per household left under the airer with a chalked floor number, Mina's uniformly folded stack on the folding table, Lena's two extra households' loads, Evelyn's wiped-down machines, Omar's deep-service oil can and the bulb he changes. And the silence where a transmitter should be: a brass signal outlet high on the wall with a cloth lead that goes nowhere, painted over (Accord 11: one anchor painted over; Bible III). The player infers the most social room in the building, used by everyone and never at the same time, and the one thing in it that cannot be explained.

observed: Large bright room, brass flush-dome light, plain tan plaster walls, bare concrete floor with no drain.
Two wringer washers: grey box tubs on cream wooden stands with wooden-roller wringers on top; no motor, hose or drain.
Two grey rinse tubs on a wooden leg frame against a white-painted brick pier; no taps, supply pipes or waste.
Ceiling airer: wooden slat rack on ropes through pulleys, cleated to the pier; flat cream cloths hang from it.
Dark green Z-braced door on the far wall; furniture is spread thinly across a very large floor.
No baskets, soap, copper, mangle table, benches or wet marks on the floor.
Defect: Rinse tubs and washers have no water supply, taps or drains; no floor drain anywhere.
Defect: Hanging cloths are flat untextured rectangles.
Defect: Walls and floor show no damp, lime or soap staining in a wet room.
interpretations: The set pieces are correct in type and read at a glance: wringers, tubs, airer.
Nothing is plumbed, so the room reads as a display rather than a wet basement laundry.
Scale is generous; the room would read fuller with the washers pulled toward the pier.

areas.group_intro: The basement. The oldest layer the player works in: the 1912 hand-fired coal boiler that was patched, re-jacketed and never replaced (Bible VIII.5.c), its coal annex with the gravity chute from the street cover (ORISON_V2_COAL_DELIVERY), the dry electrical room with the fuse panel (G05, implemented), the maintenance shop with its repair bench, toolboard and parts shelf, eighteen labelled resident storage bays, the laundry with two wringer washers, two rinse tubs and the ceiling airer (Bible VIII.5.d; T02 implemented), the reading nook with its emeralite lamp off the public core, and the service stair that continues down from F01. WORS 1610 broadcast out of this laundry from 1962 to 1999 with no transmitter ever found (Bible III); Cal is the transmitter (web I); Juno records the laundry's hum on Thursdays; Teresa has the machines to herself at 03:00 on Saturdays; Omar checks the breaker panel at 03:00 every night. The owner JSON records the boiler finishes (T01), the laundry cloth (T02) and the basement walls and service context (A04) as implemented and reviewed. The 2026-10-05 sweep's open findings for B1 were the stair underside, coal heap, alley boundaries and reading-room furniture, since addressed. What the basement still lacks is the residents' use of it: the storage bays hold nothing, the laundry has no laundry, the nook has no reader.

observed: 1.2 m corridor, plain tan plaster walls and concrete floor; no skirting, conduit or pipe runs along the walls.
Dark green-grey Z-braced metal doors with brass lever handles; fire door (DT2) closed and flush, rivet-dotted frames.
Galvanized duct drops from a square ceiling flange and elbows into the right wall above the open door (DT1); run terminates.
Public stair with marble treads and iron balusters visible at the corridor end (OV, DT3).
No corridor light fixture visible in any tile; only the hand-lamp pool lights the route.
Walls and floor show no wear, staining or scuffing along a service route.
Defect: No visible corridor light fixture despite the 'lit route' brief.
Defect: Corridor walls bare: no conduit, pipe run, skirting or wear on a plant-room approach.
interpretations: Reads as a service passage; the duct and heavy doors say plant room ahead.
Without a fixture the 'lit retreat route' is lit only by the player; a cage lamp would sell it.
Door-and-duct vocabulary is period-plausible; the emptiness of the walls is the weak point.

areas.title: The boiler room: the 1912 plant
areas.location: 6.15 x 9.5 m with the boiler on its grounded base, the water column, the breeching to the flue, the operating boiler-well window, doors to the coal room and the service stair

areas.narrative: The boiler, its firing and ash doors, the draft damper, the water glass, the breeching and the well window are installed and operate; T01's neutral iron and restrained lagging are reviewed. The room should show the firing routine's evidence: the shovel leaning by the fire door, the ash can and its ring on the floor, the clinker rake, the coal-dust fan from the coal door, a chalked log on the wall by the water column (dates and levels as strokes), the oil can and rag by the damper. Light is the plant's own: the firebox glow when open, one cage bulb. The player infers a plant kept alive by hand for sixteen years.

areas.group: BUILDING-WIDE / systemic findings and shared families
areas.title: Systemic findings that no single room can fix
areas.location: Every floor; the evidence is the room sheets named in each change
areas.narrative: The room-by-room review repeats a small number of findings in dozens of rooms. They are listed once here with stable ids so the room pages can cite them instead of restating them, and so the implementing agent can fix a family rather than a room. In order of how much they cost the building's credibility: the six completion-interior homes are furnished with copied templates (1D carries a seamstress's furniture; 1A, 3D and 4D have only a bed, wardrobe, table and chair; 3D has no range); the three converted second bedrooms are not converted; several shared furniture variants read post-1950 (tulip-pedestal round tables, chrome wire shelving, square-steel-post shelves, slab-cushion sofas); bath tile is applied to both faces of bath walls so it shows in halls and bedrooms; ventilation ducts and their hangers end in air; the service spine is a bare block-out shell with no risers, lights or finishes; windows are bare of curtains and blinds everywhere at 20:00; bedding is flat slabs; shower curtains are rigid fluted cylinders; mirrors hang tilted off walls; cold cyan light leaks around door leaves and openings with no visible source; six homes have no radio; completion-interior main rooms are lit by flush domes where every authored living room has a pendant. None of these is a texture problem; they are variant, family and data problems, which is why they are cheap to fix once and expensive to fix per room.

areas.title: The street: road, walks and traffic
areas.location: The 30 ft carriageway and both 15 ft walks between the Orison's front and the south block (Harukiya, gateway, kiosk), from the west hoarding to the east hoarding
areas.narrative: The route captures walk the north pavement from the Orison door to the bodega and back; the facade stations look at the building from the carriageway. The street works as built. At 20:00 in November it should also carry the block's trade and the day's paper: a newsstand's lit hatch (the News booth is in the Arcade; a second street kiosk is not proposed), an ash can at every areaway, horse consequence in the gutter with the restrained fly shimmer the commensals brief allows, the election's broadsides pasted on the hoarding, the laundry's steam vent on the Arcade's west flank (the Model Laundry is inside the Passage; its vent can still breathe onto the street), and sound: a train on the proposed viaduct, heard not seen (T-ENDS open question). The player infers a working Queens street that does not stop for the storm.

areas.group_intro: The street. One 30 ft road crossing with 15 ft walks, no dedicated crossing point, no death: being hit is a horn, a shove and four seconds of lost dignity (ORISON_STREET_BRIEF, built). Traffic is ten instanced kinds including a rail-less tram (the authored wrong five percent) and the rare WE TUNA PIANOS truck; night traffic reads by wet-road headlight pools; both ends are the densest part of the same storm behind wet timber hoardings (T8), with a proposed railway crossing both ends (T-ENDS, not built). The front facade, marquee, neon blade, front pavement and city shells are fitted; the gateway host and the subway kiosk stair (K0/K1) stand opposite; the bodega is at the east end of the north walk. Bible VIII.1: there are still horses on Roosevelt Avenue; VIII.4: ice and coal. The street is correct and quiet; what it lacks at 20:00 on a Saturday in November is the ordinary trade of a Queens block: a newsstand's light, steam from a laundry vent, an ash can, a horse's consequence, the election's paper.

The hero shop by owner ruling (ORISON_COMMERCIAL_DESTINATION_PLAN, 2026-08-29): counter, stools, display case, coffee urn, the cooler that hums (Juno records it), a radio, aisles of goods still advertising for manufacturers who no longer exist, the sale sign with the error Evelyn corrects in her head, the back counter of notions (fuses, washers, tape, wire) so the super's errand and the neighbours' share one room, and a receiving room behind. In 1928 the bodega sells valves in printed sleeves beside the cigarettes (Bible VIII.4) and hearing-aid batteries for Cal. The destination plan's impossible back-room link to the Arcade's service corridor is a ruled design not yet built; nothing here depends on it.

areas.group_intro: The Vantry Arcade. Eleven shops in one glass-vaulted hall behind a 6 m street portal and a 10.3 m throat: west side laundry, cobbler, locksmith, hardware, funeral; east side diner, druggist, news, pawn, radio, photo (FINAL_MAP_REDESIGN_BRIEF; VANTRY_ARCADE_RECONSTRUCTION_BRIEF V1 built the nave, clerestory, lantern and pendant clock). Three loaded handcarts, brass nosings, cast-iron edge drains and wheel wear are the finish layer; at 02:00 ten shops close behind sliding iron lattice grilles and the carts are chained; HARDWARE PAINT alone keeps night service because the Mina loop buys the capsule there (PS6). Every shop has a ledger (shop guide II.3) and a back door that says there is depth (V2 phase: rear zones as view-only). The shop guide's hero objects and flair items are largely fabricated (DOCS.md's October family records); this dossier checks each against the capture and proposes only what the guide names and the fabrication index leaves open: rear rooms, the human traces, the hours states.

areas.group_intro: The Harukiya. Otomo's basement bar transplanted under the south block and run by a Japanese operator (ledger A0.4): the teal littered descent with the soiled red rug, the battered red steel door, two receiving cabinets immediately left on entering, the long counter under its 1.76 m canopy with the rim light, the barrels and crowded pictures behind the backbar, the violet-felt pool table, the plywood stage with the phonautograph and the Songbook, the couch banks, palms, the jukebox, one tiny customer WC. The grand fabric is inherited second-hand from a closed hotel bar (A0.3); the signal machines are native and forty years early; the jukebox's records stay dated 1999-2008 as the phenomenon; the two photographs show the block in 1913 and 1919. G08-G13 (loudspeakers, piano and microphone, phonautograph, darts, receiving cabinets, signage) and the gallery, stage, pool, fixture mounts, pipe supports, ceiling finish, furniture and service access are implemented. Prohibition is not in canon; the room reads as a speakeasy for free if the owner wants it (see canon findings).

areas.group_intro: The ground floor. The address: the 1928 entrance with its transom, the sign that reads EST. 1928, the earliest photograph on the lobby wall, the lobby's sealed Vantry master clock permanently four minutes fast (Bible VIII.5.e), the brass mail bank with eighteen occupied boxes and six deliberately empty recesses (Bible IV.1), the house telephone board the player operates, the watch room with the watchman's detector clock, night register, signal register and tour key (G01-G03 implemented), the dumbwaiter on the service hall (G04), the common reading room with its oak table and bookcases, the package room's shelving, the lobby benches (public_furnishings.md) and the staff restroom. The lobby is where the schedules put the building's social life: Nadia's surgery hours at 08:15, Evelyn's noticeboard at 08:30, the Transients' almost-departure at 07:30, the tenant association on Saturdays, Cam's package handoffs at 18:00, Mae's gloved finger along the mail-bank brass. The smoke capture shows a terrazzo lobby with wainscot, two benches, two windows with brick reveals and a noticeboard, generously empty; the watch room with its instruments on bare plaster; the mail room's bank and board. The ground floor is correct and under-told: the eighteen households should be legible at the mail bank, the notices should carry the building's politics, and the vestibule should be the weather lock it is named.

areas.users: all residents, the player, the lift
areas.narrative: The stair core is the oldest thing the player touches: honed marble treads dished by sixteen years of feet, iron balusters, a rail polished gold at hand height, the enamel floor plate, the lift landing with its brass call plate and the dial above it. The lift landing is the building's most used square metre: the brass call plate, the dial, the gate rattle. The floor plate reads street/watch and service. Its unique piece: the lift inspection card. Cores carry sound up and down the building; this is where the Tenant's body is audible.

areas.title: Evelyn Marsh's vestibule
areas.location: Entry from the public hall; distributes to the main room and private hall
areas.narrative: The vestibule is the first room the player reads and the one that decides whether the flat belongs to somebody. Evelyn Marsh should be legible here before any other room: a coat on a proper hanger, galoshes paired toe-out on a drip mat, a corrected shopping list pinned at eye height, an umbrella furled and buttoned. The entry opens straight off the lobby (F01_A_ENTRY_DOOR connects F01_LOBBY), so Evelyn's threshold is the most public threshold in the building: her door mat is the one the whole lobby sees, and it is the cleanest. Three doors (main, private hall, lobby) leave one wall for the landing set. It is also where the building's own hardware shows: the 1912 brass signal outlet beside the later switch plate, the chain guard on the entry door, the painted-over bell push, the Vantry point grille on the ceiling.

areas.title: Evelyn's living room: the marking table and the properly laid tray
areas.location: 7.45 x 3.35 m front room off the vestibule, one window to the street side, doors to the kitchen and the bedroom
areas.users: Evelyn Marsh; the player on the Saturday bake round
areas.narrative: A long, narrow front room with one window. Today it holds a 5C-template table and chair and a radiator. It should hold a teacher's living room arranged in formal balance: the dining table set for one with a tray cloth and the good cup, the second cup on the dresser that nobody has used, a reading chair by the window with a floor lamp, a wireless on its table with the quiz programme she corrects aloud, and the two framed documents centred on the long wall as a pair. Everything is pre-war in cut and immaculate in keeping; the wear is the wear of thirty-one years of care, not of neglect: the chair arm polished by one hand, the table edge where the marking pencil rests, a rub on the floor where the chair is pulled out at exactly the same angle twice a day. The player should infer a woman who still keeps school hours for nobody, and who corrects the world because she cannot stop caring for it.

areas.group_intro: Evelyn Marsh, 1A. Retired teacher, plum cardigan, red pencil; the wound is that care became correction (Bible IV). Canon gives the flat formal balance, a marking desk, a tea service, corrected grocery lists, a medication organizer as the hero object and one contradiction: a spare guest cup, never once used. Her schedule is the building's clock: breakfast at a properly set table with the radio news, the bodega at 07:00, the lobby noticeboard red-pencilled at 08:30, the bake-and-deliver round on Saturdays, Peter intercepted at the mail bank at 18:00, radio quiz programmes corrected aloud in the evening, lights out by 23:00. The wardrobe bible adds the pre-war silhouette (hems never shortened, hair never cut) and a thin gold wedding band she has not removed since 1901. Proposed backstory: she married in 1901, fought the Board of Education's ban on married women teachers and kept her post; the permission letter is framed beside her retirement certificate (the decor profile's orderly pair); she was widowed before the war and the one photograph in the flat is his, because photographs are dear here. Her 1954 class register (web I) sits on the study shelf with one name underlined twice: Peter Wren's (web II.6). Build state: 1A is one of the six completion-interior homes furnished from 5C templates (a bed, a wardrobe, a table, a chair, a WC and a sink support) with flush domes in every room and no radio, no reading chair and no desk. It is spatially proven and visually anonymous.

areas.title: Evelyn Marsh's kitchen
areas.location: Off the main room through the kitchen opening
areas.narrative: The kitchen is 1890 while the parlour is 1970 (Bible VIII.4): an enamel gas range on an angle-iron base, a sink with a drainboard, a wall cupboard, the sliding preparation cabinet, an electric monitor-top on splayed legs, new, expensive, noticeably loud, and the neighbours know who has one. What makes it Evelyn Marsh's is one place laid properly at every meal: a tray cloth, the good cup and the second cup that is never used, a tea caddy with a spoon on a string. The kitchen is compact (3.1 x 2.45 m) with the sink on a drainboard and the monitor-top she keeps immaculate; the hall opening lets the kettle be heard from the bath. The ice card convention does not apply: 1A is one of the four electric flats and the neighbours know it. Light is the kitchen linear or flush dome and the window; the Vantry point on the ceiling listens to the kettle.

areas.title: Evelyn Marsh's bathroom
areas.location: Private bathroom off the unit's private hall
areas.narrative: Every V2 bathroom is a windowless 1928 reopening room on one of the four roof ventilators: a painted gravity register, a cast-iron tub or shower receptor, a pedestal basin, a mirror medicine cabinet and a flush dome. What makes this one Evelyn Marsh's is a senior's medicated routine: the medicine cabinet is the full one, a glass with a dosing spoon on the basin, a bath rail she fitted herself and keeps polished. The bath rail is hers, not the landlord's: a brass rail screwed into the tile beside the receptor with the screw heads painted to match, the only thing in the flat she fitted herself. The room should pass the Shenmue test at the basin: evidence of construction (the register and its painted-over screws), attachment (the cabinet's two fixings), use (the wiping arc on the mirror), age (crazed enamel, a hairline in the tile), maintenance (a replacement chain on the plug) and consequence (a water line on the floor where the curtain leaks).

areas.title: Teresa Vale's vestibule
areas.location: Entry from the public hall; distributes to the main room and private hall
areas.narrative: The vestibule is the first room the player reads and the one that decides whether the flat belongs to somebody. Teresa Vale should be legible here before any other room: black laced shoes already pointing at the door, the navy cape on the first hook, a crushed cap, the thermos on the shelf where a hand finds it blind. 1D's entry is on the service hall (F01_D_ENTRY_DOOR connects F01_SERVICE_HALL), not the lobby: she leaves and returns by the back of the building at 22:00 and 07:40, past the staff restroom, and never sees the lobby crowd. The vestibule is 2.0 x 2.7 m with an opening to the main room; one wall only. It is also where the building's own hardware shows: the 1912 brass signal outlet beside the later switch plate, the chain guard on the entry door, the painted-over bell push, the Vantry point grille on the ceiling.

areas.group_intro: Teresa Vale, 1D. Night nurse at St. Adjutor's, navy scrubs and cape, a dented thermos and a fob watch; the wound is that rest summons alarms (Bible IV). She sleeps ten to five, shops on the way home in yesterday's uniform, and her flat is a sparse threshold with the night-shift memory deeper inside (decor profile). Canon: the silenced alarm clock as hero object, blackout curtains and a bell she cannot unplug as the contradiction, cleanliness 0.55, thermos and leftovers in the kitchen, the office converted to a night-shift station, a hamper and an exhausted half-finished meal (lived-in brief). She is Mina's mother one floor down (web II.4); their hours never overlap, and she was on the custody ward the night Price died (web II.1). Proposed backstory: the bell she cannot unplug is a 1912 Vantry house bell wired before the building had tenants, the only one still connected; she moved the alarm clock to the icebox top the first week and has not touched it since. Build state: 1D was furnished from 2B's templates and carries Lena's fabric worktable, pattern board and two fabric shelves. A night nurse's flat currently reads as a seamstress's workroom; this is the single largest legibility defect among the eighteen homes and it is a data copy, not a design.

areas.title: Teresa Vale's kitchen
areas.location: Off the main room through the kitchen opening
areas.narrative: The kitchen is 1890 while the parlour is 1970 (Bible VIII.4): an enamel gas range on an angle-iron base, a sink with a drainboard, a wall cupboard, the sliding preparation cabinet, an oak icebox with a zinc lining, a drip tray under it that someone has to empty and an ice card in the window. What makes it Teresa Vale's is a dented vacuum flask and a dull nickel kettle, one pan, a plate of yesterday under a cloth, the alarm clock silenced on top of the icebox. A B-type kitchen with its own door off the private hall. The alarm clock on the icebox top is the hero object: silenced, where she cannot hear it from bed. Light is the kitchen linear or flush dome and the window; the Vantry point on the ceiling listens to the kettle.

areas.title: Teresa Vale's bathroom
areas.location: Private bathroom off the unit's private hall
areas.narrative: Every V2 bathroom is a windowless 1928 reopening room on one of the four roof ventilators: a painted gravity register, a cast-iron tub or shower receptor, a pedestal basin, a mirror medicine cabinet and a flush dome. What makes this one Teresa Vale's is a night worker's bathroom used at the wrong hours: towel never fully dry, blackout against the light-slot, uniform collar soaking in the basin. The bath has a window (one of the few), so the blackout extends here: a towel pegged across it. The collar and cuffs soaking in the basin are the only white things in the room. The room should pass the Shenmue test at the basin: evidence of construction (the register and its painted-over screws), attachment (the cabinet's two fixings), use (the wiping arc on the mirror), age (crazed enamel, a hairline in the tile), maintenance (a replacement chain on the plug) and consequence (a water line on the floor where the curtain leaks).

areas.narrative: The stair core is the oldest thing the player touches: honed marble treads dished by sixteen years of feet, iron balusters, a rail polished gold at hand height, the enamel floor plate, the lift landing with its brass call plate and the dial above it. The landing is the floor-and-unit decision for 2A and 2D; the lift's brass plate and dial are here. The punchlist asks each half-landing for its own piece; this landing's should be the first photograph the building owns (1928). Cores carry sound up and down the building; this is where the Tenant's body is audible.

areas.narrative: A 1912 public corridor under 1928 paint: wainscot to 1.1 m, a dado rail, the picture rail that survived the demolition, enamel floor plates in both cores, a flush dome every few metres and the apartment doors with their transoms. A hall that goes nowhere, to a door that does not open. It has its own flush dome and switch and is the quietest public space on the floor. The sealed threshold deserves the building's silence treatment (see F02_D_RESTRICTED): a paper notice, dust on the mat, no milk. The halls are where neighbours meet and where the building's own voice is loudest: a riser knocks, a door spills light, the lift gate rattles in the shaft.

areas.title: Mina Vale's vestibule
areas.location: Entry from the public hall; distributes to the main room and private hall
areas.narrative: The vestibule is the first room the player reads and the one that decides whether the flat belongs to somebody. Mina Vale should be legible here before any other room: a key board with every hook labelled, a numbered coat hook strip, a wall file of out-letters, a label on the label maker's box. A 1.95 x 2.7 m vestibule opening straight into the main room. Mina's landing set is a key board with every hook labelled and a numbered coat strip; the labels are blank card rectangles at this scale (no lettering), but the regularity reads from the door. It is also where the building's own hardware shows: the 1912 brass signal outlet beside the later switch plate, the chain guard on the entry door, the painted-over bell push, the Vantry point grille on the ceiling.

areas.group_intro: Mina Vale, 2A. Caption editor; twenty-two years a certified court reporter until four blank seconds in the record of the State ended that life (Bible IV). Her wound: everything must be annotated or it does not count; the rule she must learn is that silence does not require annotation. 2A is the complete, voiced Case 01 and the bar every other case is measured against: the failed Vantry point that chirps, the caption desk, the calibrator, the letter, the refrigerator caption residue after the first dream. Canon dressing: labelled everything, cable discipline, duplicate correction tools, measured portions, the conspicuously unlabelled box (hero object), slate tailor-made clothes and a stenographer's pencil behind the ear. Decor profile: a working wall, captions visible from the desk, the unsaid allowed one confrontational axis. Teresa is her mother one floor down and their hours never overlap (web II.4); Cal's reel two floors up holds her four seconds (web II.1). Proposed backstory: the unlabelled box holds the stenotype paper of one afternoon in court; the caption wall is pinned so that one card is blank. Build state: the richest apartment in data (desk, pinboard, lamp, papers, headphones, deck, projector, three wire shelves, sofa, radio, bookshelf, case objects) and the one whose gameplay must be preserved exactly. The main room reads under-dressed at overview distance and the wire shelving reads later than 1927; the desk is in the bedroom, which is right for a woman who works nights alone.

areas.title: Mina's living room: the working wall
areas.location: 8.1 x 6.95 m, two west windows, openings to the vestibule and kitchen, door to the private hall
areas.users: Mina Vale; the player for the whole of Case 01
areas.narrative: The largest living room in the building and the one the player studies longest. Today it holds a sofa, three wire shelving units, a round table and two chairs, a coffee table with the deck, a wireless table and radio, a projector on a stand, the repaired bookshelf and the radiator; Mina stands in it at 20:00. The walls are bare. The decor profile asks for a working wall: captions visible from the desk, images arranged so that one confrontational axis runs from the desk to the thing she never annotated. The desk is in the bedroom (right for her), so this room is the public face of her discipline: the shelves hold labelled boxes in rows with their labels facing out, every cable runs to a point and is tied, the sofa has one cushion squared and one with a dent, the coffee table carries the deck and a labelled jar of pencils; the unlabelled box sits in plain sight on the lowest shelf with its blank face forward. The player infers a woman who has annotated her whole life except one object, and that the object is the point.

areas.title: Mina Vale's kitchen
areas.location: Off the main room through the kitchen opening
areas.narrative: The kitchen is 1890 while the parlour is 1970 (Bible VIII.4): an enamel gas range on an angle-iron base, a sink with a drainboard, a wall cupboard, the sliding preparation cabinet, an electric monitor-top on splayed legs, new, expensive, noticeably loud, and the neighbours know who has one. What makes it Mina Vale's is labelled jars in rows, a kitchen scale, a measured half-loaf, the icebox shelves labelled in her own hand. Mina's kitchen carries the Case 01 refrigerator caption residue after the first wake; the fridge is a monitor-top in data where the Bible allows four electric flats (1A, 3A, 5B, 6C). Converting it to an icebox keeps the caption marker (it binds to the refrigerator marker, not the model). Light is the kitchen linear or flush dome and the window; the Vantry point on the ceiling listens to the kettle.

areas.title: Mina Vale's bathroom
areas.location: Private bathroom off the unit's private hall
areas.narrative: Every V2 bathroom is a windowless 1928 reopening room on one of the four roof ventilators: a painted gravity register, a cast-iron tub or shower receptor, a pedestal basin, a mirror medicine cabinet and a flush dome. What makes this one Mina Vale's is a single adult who keeps things exact: one toothbrush, one glass, towel squared on the rail, nothing on the floor. The smoke capture shows the standard set: pedestal basin, WC, curtain, cabinet, register. For Mina add only exactness: the toothbrush parallel to the basin edge, the towel's fold aligned to the rail end. The room should pass the Shenmue test at the basin: evidence of construction (the register and its painted-over screws), attachment (the cabinet's two fixings), use (the wiping arc on the mirror), age (crazed enamel, a hairline in the tile), maintenance (a replacement chain on the plug) and consequence (a water line on the floor where the curtain leaks).

areas.narrative: The desk, its chair, the pinboard, the green office lamp, the papers, the mug and the headphones are all here, with the bed, nightstand and wardrobe. areas.title: Lena Ortiz's vestibule
areas.location: Entry from the public hall; distributes to the main room and private hall
areas.narrative: The vestibule is the first room the player reads and the one that decides whether the flat belongs to somebody. Lena Ortiz should be legible here before any other room: a bentwood chair for a waiting client, a mirror, a pincushion on the shelf, a tape measure on the hook and a paper pattern taped to the door back. 2B's entry opens onto the service crossing, so the vestibule is the client's waiting room: a bentwood chair, a mirror, a paper pattern taped to the back of the door, the tape measure on the hook. The threshold anchor F02_B_THRESHOLD is here. It is also where the building's own hardware shows: the 1912 brass signal outlet beside the later switch plate, the chain guard on the entry door, the painted-over bell push, the Vantry point grille on the ceiling.

areas.group_intro: Lena Ortiz, 2B. Seamstress, burgundy knit, shears; she mends everyone but her own hem (Bible IV); visible repairs can hold. Canon: clients welcome at the door, a cutting table, a repair queue, fabric stored vertically, the mended upholstery armchair as hero object, the biggest pots in the building because she cooks for others, cleanliness 0.7, maintenance 0.9; one hem still pinned. Her arrival layer is 1911 and the Triangle fire (web I); she has opinions about locked doors she has never spoken aloud; she mends Cam's jersey strap without being asked (web II.5); Saturday she sits early at the Harukiya and mends the banquette's split vinyl. The sewing machine treadle is an OPERATE owner in the matrix. Proposed backstory: three garments in the repair queue are from this building, tagged with floor numbers instead of names. Build state: B-type plan (vestibule, main with openings, kitchen, private hall, bed, bath), the fabric worktable, pattern board, patterns, notions, two fabric shelves in the hall, a radio. The furniture is hers; the room needs the queue, the machine and the chair.

areas.title: Lena Ortiz's bathroom
areas.location: Private bathroom off the unit's private hall
areas.narrative: Every V2 bathroom is a windowless 1928 reopening room on one of the four roof ventilators: a painted gravity register, a cast-iron tub or shower receptor, a pedestal basin, a mirror medicine cabinet and a flush dome. What makes this one Lena Ortiz's is a single adult's ordinary use: one of everything, a second towel that is really a floorcloth. The bath has a window; a darned stocking dries on the rail (wardrobe bible: one darned at the heel). The room should pass the Shenmue test at the basin: evidence of construction (the register and its painted-over screws), attachment (the cabinet's two fixings), use (the wiping arc on the mirror), age (crazed enamel, a hairline in the tile), maintenance (a replacement chain on the plug) and consequence (a water line on the floor where the curtain leaks).

areas.title: Juno Kells's vestibule
areas.location: Entry from the public hall; distributes to the main room and private hall
areas.narrative: The vestibule is the first room the player reads and the one that decides whether the flat belongs to somebody. Juno Kells should be legible here before any other room: cable cases stacked against the wall, a man's ulster on the hook, headphones hung by the cable, takeout menus under a magnet on the door. 2C's entry opens directly off the public core, so the cable cases stacked inside the door are heard being dragged across the landing at 02:00. The ulster on the hook is a man's. It is also where the building's own hardware shows: the 1912 brass signal outlet beside the later switch plate, the chain guard on the entry door, the painted-over bell push, the Vantry point grille on the ceiling.

areas.group_intro: Juno Kells, 2C. Audio artist, asymmetric crop, recorder (a Rule-of-Signal device, licensed early); her work was taken and the feedback became load-bearing; connection requires an open channel (Bible IV.1, a case). Canon: a working musician's entry, the second bedroom converted to a recording room with blankets fixed to the walls and a stolen session archive (hero object), cable management as the one meticulous thing in a room of chaos, takeout and coffee, the range used as a shelf for tape boxes, cleanliness 0.38, nocturnal; she samples others without asking and take 18 of Rhea's session lives in her archive (web II.7); she roof-records Mon/Wed and visits Cal to trade tapes on Saturdays. Proposed backstory: one reel box is labelled only with a 1927 date. Build state: a completion-interior C-type home with two made beds, two nightstands, a dining set, a colour board, a bookshelf and a wireless table, and a studio closet holding two wardrobes. No recording room exists; the second bedroom is a second bedroom.

areas.title: Juno Kells's bathroom
areas.location: Private bathroom off the unit's private hall
areas.narrative: Every V2 bathroom is a windowless 1928 reopening room on one of the four roof ventilators: a painted gravity register, a cast-iron tub or shower receptor, a pedestal basin, a mirror medicine cabinet and a flush dome. What makes this one Juno Kells's is a single adult's ordinary use: one of everything, a second towel that is really a floorcloth. Yesterday's kohl on the basin edge; a silver ear cuff on the shelf (wardrobe bible). The room should pass the Shenmue test at the basin: evidence of construction (the register and its painted-over screws), attachment (the cabinet's two fixings), use (the wiping arc on the mirror), age (crazed enamel, a hairline in the tile), maintenance (a replacement chain on the plug) and consequence (a water line on the floor where the curtain leaks).

areas.title: F03 east hall: the approach to Omar
areas.location: From the core east to the service crossing
areas.narrative: A 1912 public corridor under 1928 paint: wainscot to 1.1 m, a dado rail, the picture rail that survived the demolition, enamel floor plates in both cores, a flush dome every few metres and the apartment doors with their transoms. A hall where things wait for the super: a radiator section on the floor against the wall, a labelled parts bag hung on the dado, a crate of somebody's broken lamp. Nothing in the route. The halls are where neighbours meet and where the building's own voice is loudest: a riser knocks, a door spills light, the lift gate rattles in the shaft.

areas.group_intro: Malcolm Reed, 3A. Horticulturist, moss silhouette, secateurs in a hip sheath, earth under the nails; he kept a cutting alive so a goodbye would not finish; compost is transformation (Bible IV). Canon: a propagation shelf at the window light, a pruning station, reused jars, a soil-tracked entry, a compost pail under the sink, the empty memorial pot on the sill above the sink (hero object), one shelf spot kept clear and dusted and never filled (contradiction), cleanliness 0.6, early sleeper, the monitor-top kept since it was new (one of the four). His layer is 1918 (web I): the cutting came from a windowsill geranium the morning of a goodbye the influenza did not let him finish, to Auggie Reed, whose name he took; Sacha (6A) is Auggie's line and photographs his plants on Sundays (web II.8). He works the parks greenhouse by day, the roof beds at dawn and dusk, and hands out rooted cuttings on Saturdays so everyone in the building has a descendant of the same plant. Proposed backstory: the empty pot stands where the plant would have been happiest; the geranium itself is the story specimen and is never named. Build state: the main room already carries the potting bench, specimen, cuttings, seed jars, radio and a repaired bookshelf; it needs the propagation shelf at the window, the jars everywhere and the one clear place.

areas.title: Malcolm Reed's bathroom
areas.location: Private bathroom off the unit's private hall
areas.narrative: Every V2 bathroom is a windowless 1928 reopening room on one of the four roof ventilators: a painted gravity register, a cast-iron tub or shower receptor, a pedestal basin, a mirror medicine cabinet and a flush dome. What makes this one Malcolm Reed's is a single adult's ordinary use: one of everything, a second towel that is really a floorcloth. Soil in the basin trap, a nail brush, hands that never come clean (wardrobe bible); the punchlist's F03_A_BATH toilet-in-shower overlap was a V1 row and must be rechecked in the capture. The room should pass the Shenmue test at the basin: evidence of construction (the register and its painted-over screws), attachment (the cabinet's two fixings), use (the wiping arc on the mirror), age (crazed enamel, a hairline in the tile), maintenance (a replacement chain on the plug) and consequence (a water line on the floor where the curtain leaks).

areas.location: Entry from the public hall; distributes to the main room and private hall
areas.narrative: The vestibule is the first room the player reads and the one that decides whether the flat belongs to somebody. Omar Bell should be legible here before any other room: boots on a tray, the apron hung in frame with its tools in it, a parts bag, a pegboard of other people's keys with tags. 2.0 x 2.7 m off the service crossing: boots on a tray, the ochre apron hung in frame with tools in its pockets (wardrobe bible late-night state), a parts bag, and a pegboard of other people's keys with tags. This is the building's service entrance in miniature. It is also where the building's own hardware shows: the 1912 brass signal outlet beside the later switch plate, the chain guard on the entry door, the painted-over bell push, the Vantry point grille on the ceiling.

areas.group_intro: Omar Bell, 3B. Repair technician and the building's super in all but title; an apron of categorized tools; he cannot declare anything unrepairable (Bible IV.1, a case: appliances arriving from incorrect timelines). Canon: repair intake and outgoing zones, labelled fastener drawers, a service aisle, boots and toolbelt at the door, two of every appliance with one half torn down on newspaper, the sacrificial teardown appliance as hero object kept broken on purpose for parts and company, cleanliness 0.8, maintenance 0.98, early sleeper who wakes at 03:00 to check the B1 breaker panel. Married to Iris (5C) since 1977 and not in the same room since the blackout (web II.3); his notes to the super are notes to himself; Tuesday nights he re-caps Cal's chassis in 5B; Thursday mornings he does the Iris round while she is out by arrangement. Proposed backstory: the sacrificial teardown is a radio chassis from the night of the 1977 blackout. Build state: the densest workroom in data (workbench, two tool shelves, toolboard, parts crate, trays, jars, manuals, coil, bench lamp, wall radio, projector) with a service door from the kitchen onto the south service hall. The alcove wardrobe shows its unfinished back to the main room (punchlist). It needs the intake/outgoing logic and the teardown.

areas.narrative: The workbench, two tool shelves, toolboard, parts crate, trays, jars, manuals, coil, the friction bench lamp, the wall radio and the projector are installed; the room is already the most specific in data. The logic the lived-in brief asks for is intake on one side, outgoing on the other, the bench between, and a clear service aisle: a crate by the door labelled with tags for things waiting diagnosis (story panel), a shelf of repaired things wrapped and tagged for return, and on newspaper on the floor the sacrificial teardown: a radio chassis half dismantled with its screws in a saucer, kept that way. Two of every appliance. The player infers a man who repairs everyone's things, keeps one broken for company, and whose home is maintained to a degree nobody else's is.

areas.title: Omar Bell's kitchen
areas.location: Off the main room through the kitchen opening
areas.narrative: The kitchen is 1890 while the parlour is 1970 (Bible VIII.4): an enamel gas range on an angle-iron base, a sink with a drainboard, a wall cupboard, the sliding preparation cabinet, an oak icebox with a zinc lining, a drip tray under it that someone has to empty and an ice card in the window. What makes it Omar Bell's is two of every appliance, one working and one half torn down on newspaper with its screws in a saucer; a lid gasket replaced, labelled with the date. The only kitchen with a service door onto the spine (F03_B_SERVICE_DOOR): a workshop-enamel range (Appliance Bible IV: masking-tape residue, marker numbering, one panel replaced in mismatched paint) and a lid gasket replaced and dated. The kitchen linear light is his own fitting. Light is the kitchen linear or flush dome and the window; the Vantry point on the ceiling listens to the kettle.

areas.title: Omar Bell's bathroom
areas.location: Private bathroom off the unit's private hall
areas.narrative: Every V2 bathroom is a windowless 1928 reopening room on one of the four roof ventilators: a painted gravity register, a cast-iron tub or shower receptor, a pedestal basin, a mirror medicine cabinet and a flush dome. What makes this one Omar Bell's is a practical single adult: a nail brush, a pumice, carbolic soap, a shaving mirror hung where the light actually falls. The one bathroom lit by a sconce globe instead of a dome: his own fitting. A shaving mirror hung where the sconce falls; a pumice; carbolic soap; the punchlist's toilet-in-shower overlap row must be rechecked in the capture. The room should pass the Shenmue test at the basin: evidence of construction (the register and its painted-over screws), attachment (the cabinet's two fixings), use (the wiping arc on the mirror), age (crazed enamel, a hairline in the tile), maintenance (a replacement chain on the plug) and consequence (a water line on the floor where the curtain leaks).

areas.title: Rhea Sato's vestibule
areas.location: Entry from the public hall; distributes to the main room and private hall
areas.narrative: The vestibule is the first room the player reads and the one that decides whether the flat belongs to somebody. Rhea Sato should be legible here before any other room: a dressing mirror turned to the door, a hat stand with three cloches, a scarf over the mirror corner, a shoe tree. A 2.6 x 2.7 m vestibule with three doors (entry, main, private hall): the dressing mirror turned to the door, a hat stand with three cloches, a shoe tree. The A-type plan gives her a proper entrance and she uses it as a stage wing. It is also where the building's own hardware shows: the 1912 brass signal outlet beside the later switch plate, the chain guard on the entry door, the painted-over bell push, the Vantry point grille on the ceiling.

areas.group_intro: Rhea Sato, 3D. Vocal coach and recording artist, severe bob, tuning fork on a neck chain; her mistakes accumulate as a captive note; imperfection can be voluntary (sanctioned expansion). Canon: an edit desk, take sheets, a hydration station, thrift-glam entry, a voice-care bathroom, tea, honey and lemon in a spotless never-used kitchen, no television, the isolated microphone case as hero object, a dressing mirror facing away from the booth (contradiction), the office converted to a vocal booth, cleanliness 0.65. She deleted take 18 and it survives in Juno's archive one floor down (web II.7). At 20:00 she files the day's sessions in the error archive. Proposed backstory: the error archive is a card index in a cabinet with a drawer per flaw. Build state: an A-type completion home furnished from 5C templates (bed, wardrobe, table, chair, WC, sink) with a monitor-top where the Bible allows an icebox and an empty study. Nothing says a singer lives here.

areas.narrative: The kitchen is 1890 while the parlour is 1970 (Bible VIII.4): an enamel gas range on an angle-iron base, a sink with a drainboard, a wall cupboard, the sliding preparation cabinet, an electric monitor-top on splayed legs, new, expensive, noticeably loud, and the neighbours know who has one. areas.title: Rhea Sato's bathroom

areas.narrative: Every V2 bathroom is a windowless 1928 reopening room on one of the four roof ventilators: a painted gravity register, a cast-iron tub or shower receptor, a pedestal basin, a mirror medicine cabinet and a flush dome. What makes this one Rhea Sato's is a singer's throat routine: steam kettle on the floor, a jar of pastilles, a mentholated inhaler, two glasses (gargle and rinse). A singer's bathroom: the steam kettle, pastilles, an inhaler, two glasses. The punchlist's magenta hamper intersecting a tan box was a V1 row; recheck. The room should pass the Shenmue test at the basin: evidence of construction (the register and its painted-over screws), attachment (the cabinet's two fixings), use (the wiping arc on the mirror), age (crazed enamel, a hairline in the tile), maintenance (a replacement chain on the plug) and consequence (a water line on the floor where the curtain leaks).

areas.title: Peter Wren's vestibule
areas.location: Entry from the public hall; distributes to the main room and private hall
areas.narrative: The vestibule is the first room the player reads and the one that decides whether the flat belongs to somebody. Peter Wren should be legible here before any other room: an umbrella in a drip tray that has overflowed into a tide mark, brown Oxfords with the heel worn on the outside, a hat a size out on the shelf, a stamped envelope not yet posted. 2.0 x 2.7 m off the service crossing: the umbrella in its drip tray with a tide mark on the floor, Oxfords with the heel worn outside, a derby a size out on the shelf, a stamped envelope not yet posted. The grid starts here: everything square to the wall. It is also where the building's own hardware shows: the 1912 brass signal outlet beside the later switch plate, the chain guard on the entry door, the painted-over bell push, the Vantry point grille on the ceiling.

areas.group_intro: Peter Wren, 4A. Legal clerk, rumpled brown sack suit cut in 1919, an overfilled pocket-book distending the breast pocket; every uncertainty demands another form; uncertainty does not prevent action (Bible I: the ordained second case). Canon: document staging by status, a date stamp, municipal binders, careful shoe placement, an umbrella drip tray that has overflowed, identical weekday meals in identical tins, a toaster with a replacement form taped to it that was never filed, cleanliness 0.88, the unresolved form 11-B at every station (hero object and contradiction). Decor profile: a measured grid, submission and uncertainty aligned almost too carefully. He was the clerk on the Price appeal who certified the irregularity to death (web II.1); Evelyn taught him and the note reading See me is in the wallet (web II.6); he checks the mail bank at 07:40 and 18:05 so that nothing can arrive unobserved; Saturdays the luncheonette's third stool, same order since 1924. Proposed backstory: every unresolved form is the same form at different stages. Build state: a B-type home with the writing table, dining set, wireless table, radio, sectional bookshelf and story briefs already installed; it needs the staging, the grid and the tray.

areas.narrative: The writing table, the round dining table and two chairs, the wireless table and radio, the sectional bookshelf and the story briefs are installed. The room should be a measured grid: the writing table square to the window with document stacks staged by status (in, pending, re-check) each under a brass weight, the date stamp and ink pad aligned to the blotter edge, municipal binders in a row with their spines flush, the two framed pieces (submission and uncertainty) hung on one centreline almost too carefully (decor profile), a drip tray under the radiator valve, and at this station too an unresolved form 11-B, face up. The player infers a man who files to avoid deciding, and that the grid is the deciding he can do.

areas.location: Between the main room, bedroom and bathroom
areas.narrative: A short distribution hall between bed and bath. It should not be dressed; it should be used. For Peter Wren: the hall is authored for document storage: a stack of binder boxes squared against the wall, a form 11-B on top; the shoe tree and a brush on a hook. areas.title: Peter Wren's bathroom
areas.location: Private bathroom off the unit's private hall
areas.narrative: Every V2 bathroom is a windowless 1928 reopening room on one of the four roof ventilators: a painted gravity register, a cast-iron tub or shower receptor, a pedestal basin, a mirror medicine cabinet and a flush dome. What makes this one Peter Wren's is a single adult who keeps things exact: one toothbrush, one glass, towel squared on the rail, nothing on the floor. A bath with a window; a celluloid collar drying on the rail; a form 11-B on the cistern lid (the bathroom station). The room should pass the Shenmue test at the basin: evidence of construction (the register and its painted-over screws), attachment (the cabinet's two fixings), use (the wiping arc on the mirror), age (crazed enamel, a hairline in the tile), maintenance (a replacement chain on the plug) and consequence (a water line on the floor where the curtain leaks).

areas.title: the player's vestibule
areas.location: Entry from the public hall; distributes to the main room and private hall
areas.narrative: The vestibule is the first room the player reads and the one that decides whether the flat belongs to somebody. the player should be legible here before any other room: a service cap, the maintenance keyring on a nail, a stack of printed slips under a brass weight, the drip of the carried set's battery case on the mat. The punchlist names this one of the only two undressed rooms in the building (0.54 records per square metre median; here zero). The operator's landing set: a service cap, the maintenance keyring on a nail, printed slips under a brass weight, a drip on the mat from the carried set's battery case. It is also where the building's own hardware shows: the 1912 brass signal outlet beside the later switch plate, the chain guard on the entry door, the painted-over bell push, the Vantry point grille on the ceiling.

areas.group_intro: 4B, the player. Night maintenance; the desk is the tidiest thing in the flat (Bible IV) and the case wall is tidier still (life profile contradiction). Canon: the operator's entry, kettle-toaster survival in the kitchen with the landlord's portable fan, the ordinary eight-day drop-octagon clock that must be wound (Bible VIII.5.e), the Vantry signal terminal and desk zone, the bespoke wake bed and nightstand in the alcove, the closet with its equipment shelf, the brass mail box 4B downstairs, the carried service set. 4B is where every dream ends and every shift begins; the alcove bed is the authored bedside. Mara Chen was the previous night tenant of 4B and is still on hold on the line (web II.9). Proposed backstory: she left one thing in the closet: a service cap with the wrong initials inside the band. Build state: complete in function (desk, bed, kitchen, bath, closet) and the punchlist's only undressed rooms are its closet and vestibule; the landlord's enamel task lamp is fitted; the 4B kitchen has the C1 roach scatter at the switch.

areas.title: 4B living room: the desk and the case wall
areas.location: 8.1 x 7.3 m, two windows, openings to vestibule and kitchen, door to the private hall
areas.users: the player; callers on the line
areas.narrative: The terminal desk, its chair, the couch, shelf, meal table and chairs, coffee table, wireless table and radio, the projector on its stand and the landlord's enamel lamp are installed. The desk is the tidiest thing in the flat and the case wall must be tidier: the wall behind the desk carrying the case cards in a grid under the pinboard law, with the Vantry terminal and the dial-less house telephone beside it; the rest of the room lived in badly by someone who sleeps at odd hours: a blanket on the couch, a mug ring on the coffee table, a slip stuck in the radio's grille. The drop-octagon clock on the wall where the desk chair can see it (it must be wound; hold E). The punchlist's featureless white box must be identified in the capture. The player infers themselves, and that the only order in their life is on the wall.

areas.narrative: The kitchen is 1890 while the parlour is 1970 (Bible VIII.4): an enamel gas range on an angle-iron base, a sink with a drainboard, a wall cupboard, the sliding preparation cabinet, an oak icebox with a zinc lining, a drip tray under it that someone has to empty and an ice card in the window. What makes it the player's is a kettle and a toaster on a counter otherwise bare, a tin of biscuits, the landlord's portable fan, slips and carbons under the bread board. The kettle and toaster on a counter otherwise bare; the landlord's portable fan on the floor by the opening (box fan, OPERATE); a tin of biscuits; the C1 roach scatter at the switch is landed and must stay. A trash can is one of the 4B semantic requirements. Light is the kitchen linear or flush dome and the window; the Vantry point on the ceiling listens to the kettle.

areas.title: the player's bathroom
areas.location: Private bathroom off the unit's private hall
areas.narrative: Every V2 bathroom is a windowless 1928 reopening room on one of the four roof ventilators: a painted gravity register, a cast-iron tub or shower receptor, a pedestal basin, a mirror medicine cabinet and a flush dome. What makes this one the player's is a single adult's ordinary use: one of everything, a second towel that is really a floorcloth. A window bath; the player's own: a razor, a tin of tooth powder, the towel never squared. The room should pass the Shenmue test at the basin: evidence of construction (the register and its painted-over screws), attachment (the cabinet's two fixings), use (the wiping arc on the mirror), age (crazed enamel, a hairline in the tile), maintenance (a replacement chain on the plug) and consequence (a water line on the floor where the curtain leaks).

areas.group_intro: Cam Ortiz and Noel Price, 4C. Two residents, two bedrooms, one negotiated table (hero object): a courier who is never fully still (maroon shell, satchel, knickerbockers, rest reads as collapse) and a museum preparator (indigo chore coat, white cotton gloves in the pocket, use and change are forms of love). Canon: shared territories, Cam's route by movement and Noel's objects in a museum-calm bay, bike versus gloves at the door, quick food versus preserved in the kitchen with a dead icebox on Noel's side nobody empties, a battered copper kettle both use, split sleep, cleanliness 0.5. Cam is Lena's kin and she mends the jersey strap (web II.5); Noel is the convicted man's son and has preserved the family flat into a museum (web II.1); Jonah, his brother, brings two coffees to the doorway at Sunday noon. Proposed backstory: a chalk line under the oilcloth divides the table; Noel's shelf holds three objects from the family flat before the trial. Build state: a C-type completion home with two beds correctly kept, a dining set, bookshelf, colour board and wireless table; no radio; the studio closet holds two wardrobes. It needs the division made visible.

areas.narrative: The kitchen is 1890 while the parlour is 1970 (Bible VIII.4): an enamel gas range on an angle-iron base, a sink with a drainboard, a wall cupboard, the sliding preparation cabinet, an oak icebox with a zinc lining, a drip tray under it that someone has to empty and an ice card in the window. What makes it Cam Ortiz and Noel Price's is one side of the counter quick food in paper, the other side preserved and labelled; a dead icebox nobody empties; a battered copper kettle both use. One kitchen, two centuries: Cam's side quick food in paper, Noel's side preserved and labelled; the icebox is dead on Noel's side and nobody empties the tray (a dry tray, a dust line); the battered copper kettle both use. Light is the kitchen linear or flush dome and the window; the Vantry point on the ceiling listens to the kettle.

areas.narrative: Every V2 bathroom is a windowless 1928 reopening room on one of the four roof ventilators: a painted gravity register, a cast-iron tub or shower receptor, a pedestal basin, a mirror medicine cabinet and a flush dome. What makes this one Cam Ortiz and Noel Price's is two adults who do not share: two of everything on opposite sides, two towels on separate hooks, a tape line nobody admits to. Two of everything on opposite sides of the basin; two towels on separate hooks; a tape line on the shelf nobody admits to. areas.group_intro: The Transient Guests, 4D. A replaceable pair with mismatched luggage and a railway cloakroom ticket knotted to a buttonhole; perpetual departure postpones the decision; departure is a decision (Bible IV). Canon: hotel wayfinding (impersonal reassurance visible from the exit), host-generic furniture, duplicate house-rules cards, prior guests' lost property (hero object), inadequate cookware, a cold icebox, rolling luggage, no personal history at all (contradiction), the office converted to a locked owner closet, sleep varies. They were the first tenants in 1908 and are still checking in (web I); every morning at 07:30 they stand in the lobby with coats on facing the doors; Saturdays they ask for a bill at a desk that has none. Proposed backstory: the locked closet holds nine previous guests' lost property, each tagged with a date and the room number 4D. Build state: an A-type completion home with 5C templates and a monitor-top where the Bible allows an icebox; the study has a door and no lock; nothing in it is a rental yet.

areas.title: the Transient Guests's bathroom
areas.location: Private bathroom off the unit's private hall
areas.narrative: Every V2 bathroom is a windowless 1928 reopening room on one of the four roof ventilators: a painted gravity register, a cast-iron tub or shower receptor, a pedestal basin, a mirror medicine cabinet and a flush dome. What makes this one the Transient Guests's is a short-let bathroom: hotel-issue soap, one thin towel each, a house-rules card about the bath, nothing of anybody's. Hotel-issue soap, one thin towel each, one of them clearly the building's (wardrobe bible), a rules card about the bath. The room should pass the Shenmue test at the basin: evidence of construction (the register and its painted-over screws), attachment (the cabinet's two fixings), use (the wiping arc on the mirror), age (crazed enamel, a hairline in the tile), maintenance (a replacement chain on the plug) and consequence (a water line on the floor where the curtain leaks).

areas.group_intro: Nadia Quell, 5A. Architect who became the building's live-in manager and organizes its tenants against her own employers, the Kessler Estate (Bible VI.3, ruled); she signs the player's welcome letter Management; she was silenced about violations once; name the violation. Canon: a plan wall, code books, emergency supplies, measured egress at the entry, efficient batching in the kitchen, the corrected floor plan of this building on the icebox door (hero object), the exit route measured, marked and blocked by nothing (contradiction: rehearsed), cleanliness 0.85, maintenance 0.9. Decor profile: an advocacy board, people and plans displayed like promises with room to annotate. She takes tea with Mae on Thursdays and neither says the thing (web II.2); she posts the tenant memo on her night round; she holds surgery hours in the lobby at 08:15; she is in Photo Supplies more than she is upstairs. Proposed backstory: her corrected plan shows a room that is not on the blockout. Build state: the richest study in data (plan shelf, model table, site model, pins) and a main room with a plantable, stool, pins, floor stack, papers, the counterweight lamp and a plain bookshelf. It needs the wall and the egress.

areas.users: Nadia Quell; the tenants she organizes
areas.narrative: The dining set, plantable, stool, pins, floor stack, papers, mugs, the counterweight lamp, bookshelf and radio are installed. Decor profile: an advocacy board, people and plans displayed like promises with room to annotate. The wall opposite the window should carry the plan wall: the building's drawings pinned in a row with annotations, the tenant memo drafts, the rent-strike ledger on the table (20:00: Estate correspondence answered as Management), code books on the bookshelf, a tin of emergency supplies (candles, a wrench, bandages) by the door. The plantable (an architect's drawing table) should stand at the window with its lamp. The player infers the manager who is the tenants' organizer against her own employer, and that nothing in her flat is where it could fall on anyone.

areas.title: Nadia Quell's kitchen
areas.location: Off the main room through the kitchen opening
areas.narrative: The kitchen is 1890 while the parlour is 1970 (Bible VIII.4): an enamel gas range on an angle-iron base, a sink with a drainboard, a wall cupboard, the sliding preparation cabinet, an oak icebox with a zinc lining, a drip tray under it that someone has to empty and an ice card in the window. What makes it Nadia Quell's is batch cooking: four identical covered dishes, a corrected floor plan of this building pinned to the icebox door, a tin of candles and matches. A small kitchen with a door to the study: four identical covered dishes, and on the icebox door the corrected floor plan of this building (hero object), held by two magnets. Light is the kitchen linear or flush dome and the window; the Vantry point on the ceiling listens to the kettle.

areas.title: Nadia Quell's bathroom
areas.location: Private bathroom off the unit's private hall
areas.narrative: Every V2 bathroom is a windowless 1928 reopening room on one of the four roof ventilators: a painted gravity register, a cast-iron tub or shower receptor, a pedestal basin, a mirror medicine cabinet and a flush dome. What makes this one Nadia Quell's is a practical single adult: a nail brush, a pumice, carbolic soap, a shaving mirror hung where the light actually falls. A bath with a window; the oxblood lip on a towel edge; a nail brush; the fob of keys on the cabinet knob. The room should pass the Shenmue test at the basin: evidence of construction (the register and its painted-over screws), attachment (the cabinet's two fixings), use (the wiping arc on the mirror), age (crazed enamel, a hairline in the tile), maintenance (a replacement chain on the plug) and consequence (a water line on the floor where the curtain leaks).

areas.title: Cal Dwyer's vestibule
areas.location: Entry from the public hall; distributes to the main room and private hall
areas.narrative: The vestibule is the first room the player reads and the one that decides whether the flat belongs to somebody. Cal Dwyer should be legible here before any other room: coils of aerial wire, insulators in a cigar box, a battery case on charge with a cloth lead to the signal outlet, a flat cap. 2.8 x 2.5 m with the bath door opening off it (the B-type variant): coils of aerial wire, insulators in a cigar box, a battery case on charge with a cloth lead to the signal outlet, the flat cap. The aerial wire enters through a drilled hole beside the door (see F05_WEST_HALL-003). It is also where the building's own hardware shows: the 1912 brass signal outlet beside the later switch plate, the chain guard on the entry door, the painted-over bell push, the Vantry point grille on the ceiling.

areas.group_intro: Cal Dwyer, 5B. Radio collector, mustard cardigan with one pocket sagging under a battery case, a black Bakelite hearing-aid receiver on a brown cloth cord (a Rule-of-Signal device); perfect tuning preserves moments by preventing them ending; presence is not preservation (Bible IV.1, a case). Canon: a listening triangle, a repair mat, antenna experiments at the door, catalogued tapes, a chair worn toward the radio and not the television (hero object and contradiction), the range as a stand for three console radios, the icebox holding batteries and film, the reel deck the only warm thing, cleanliness 0.45, nocturnal, dozes in the chair. He is the WORS transmitter that walked in on two legs in 1962 and stopped in 1999 (web I); his Delayed Voice Reel holds Mina's four seconds (web II.1; never rendered audible, Bible VII.8); Juno trades tapes with him on Saturdays and Omar re-caps a chassis in situ on Tuesdays. Proposed backstory: the reel is a plain box among the dated tapes with a courthouse date. Build state: a story radio, headphones and lead in the main room, two radios on the hob and a comparison table in the kitchen; a monitor-top (one of the four). The listening triangle and the worn chair do not exist.

areas.narrative: The round dining table and chairs, the wireless table with the story radio, headphones and lead, and the domestic radio are installed. The room should be the listening triangle: the chair worn toward the radio (hero object), the reel deck the only warm thing on its own table, and the main set at the third point, with the headphones' lead running across the floor where he dozes; a repair mat on the dining table with a chassis on it (Tuesday's); the tape catalogue on shelves in dated rows, one plain box among them with a courthouse date (proposed; never audible). The player infers a man who keeps moments by never letting them end, and whose chair faces the wrong way.

The range is a stand for radios (two hob radios and the comparison table are installed: correct); the monitor-top is one of the four and holds batteries and film; one bowl, one spoon, the kettle warm. Light is the kitchen linear or flush dome and the window; the Vantry point on the ceiling listens to the kettle.

areas.title: Cal Dwyer's bathroom
areas.location: Private bathroom off the unit's private hall
areas.narrative: Every V2 bathroom is a windowless 1928 reopening room on one of the four roof ventilators: a painted gravity register, a cast-iron tub or shower receptor, a pedestal basin, a mirror medicine cabinet and a flush dome. What makes this one Cal Dwyer's is a single adult's ordinary use: one of everything, a second towel that is really a floorcloth. The bath opens off the vestibule, not the hall: the receiver, cord and battery case coiled on the shelf, the only image of him without it (wardrobe bible). The room should pass the Shenmue test at the basin: evidence of construction (the register and its painted-over screws), attachment (the cabinet's two fixings), use (the wiping arc on the mirror), age (crazed enamel, a hairline in the tile), maintenance (a replacement chain on the plug) and consequence (a water line on the floor where the curtain leaks).

areas.group_intro: Iris Bell, 5C. Painter, printed headscarf, paint-ruined overalls worn out of doors; imagined audiences hold every brush; creation need not perform (Bible IV). Canon: a pigment station, a drying rack, canvas storage, paint tracked from the door, a brush-washing basin, meals between coats, failed canvases facing the wall (hero object), the second bedroom converted to a painting studio, cleanliness 0.4. Decor profile: a private gallery, self and impossible space sharing one clean wall as a diptych. Married to Omar since 1977 and two floors from him since the blackout (web II.3); Sacha photographs her canvases on Sundays, the only lens she permits; she sings two songs at the Harukiya on Fridays, magnificently, and leaves. Proposed backstory: the failed canvases are portraits of one man. Build state: a C-type completion home with a colour board, solvents and studies in the main room, a second made bed in BED2 and two wardrobes in the studio closet. No studio exists.

areas.title: Iris Bell's kitchen
areas.location: Off the main room through the kitchen opening
areas.narrative: The kitchen is 1890 while the parlour is 1970 (Bible VIII.4): an enamel gas range on an angle-iron base, a sink with a drainboard, a wall cupboard, the sliding preparation cabinet, an oak icebox with a zinc lining, a drip tray under it that someone has to empty and an ice card in the window. What makes it Iris Bell's is paint on the handles, a burner used as a brush-drying rack, a plate with a thumbprint of viridian, a loaf going hard. areas.title: Iris Bell's bathroom
areas.location: Private bathroom off the unit's private hall
areas.narrative: Every V2 bathroom is a windowless 1928 reopening room on one of the four roof ventilators: a painted gravity register, a cast-iron tub or shower receptor, a pedestal basin, a mirror medicine cabinet and a flush dome. What makes this one Iris Bell's is a painter's basin: turpentine jar, brushes bristle-up in a tin, pigment stain in the enamel crazing, a rag on the taps. A painter's basin: turpentine jar, brushes in a tin, pigment stain in the enamel crazing, paint on the taps that never comes off. The room should pass the Shenmue test at the basin: evidence of construction (the register and its painted-over screws), attachment (the cabinet's two fixings), use (the wiping arc on the mirror), age (crazed enamel, a hairline in the tile), maintenance (a replacement chain on the plug) and consequence (a water line on the floor where the curtain leaks).

areas.users: all residents, the player, the lift

areas.group_intro: Sacha Reed, 6A. Photographer-documentarian (they/them), camera and adapter tangle, no camera body visible on the person; the recording displaced the experience; experience can precede proof (Bible IV). Canon: the living room treated as a photo workspace with a backdrop rail, a charging bench and contact sheets, cases stacked at the door, no sofa and no television, eats standing at a counter used as a light table, nocturnal, one practical folding chair in a room built for an audience of lenses (contradiction), the contact sheet of the motif as hero object, cleanliness 0.55. In this world photography is dear and recording is cheap (Bible VIII.4), so every print here is money. Sacha is Auggie Reed's line and photographs Malcolm's plants on Sundays (web II.8), Iris's canvases, and the singers at the Harukiya on Fridays; night photography of the building Mon/Wed and the roof Tue/Thu. Proposed backstory: the one print of a plant in the flat is Malcolm's geranium. Build state: the main room has the tripod, two softboxes, a gear crate, two coils, a round table, radio and repaired bookshelf; the study has the desk wall with headphones, cans, papers and a mug (the punchlist's monitor overlap row belongs here). No backdrop rail, no light table, no chair.

areas.title: Sacha Reed's bathroom
areas.location: Private bathroom off the unit's private hall
areas.narrative: Every V2 bathroom is a windowless 1928 reopening room on one of the four roof ventilators: a painted gravity register, a cast-iron tub or shower receptor, a pedestal basin, a mirror medicine cabinet and a flush dome. What makes this one Sacha Reed's is a single adult's ordinary use: one of everything, a second towel that is really a floorcloth. A window bath that doubles as a darkroom rinse: a developing tray in the receptor, a red bulb jar on a nail (unlit), a strap on the hook. The room should pass the Shenmue test at the basin: evidence of construction (the register and its painted-over screws), attachment (the cabinet's two fixings), use (the wiping arc on the mirror), age (crazed enamel, a hairline in the tile), maintenance (a replacement chain on the plug) and consequence (a water line on the floor where the curtain leaks).

areas.group_intro: Jonah Price, 6B. Insomniac writer, navy dressing gown as the outfit, an annotated notebook in the pocket, a week unshaven; endings avoided until they bite; endings do not erase continuation (Bible IV; VI.6 proposes the spine is can't finish). Canon: a writing sightline from the bed, a task lamp, a draft archive, bookstore receipts, cold-drink rings on every surface, the wastebasket of rejected endings (hero object), the bed facing the desk so the last thing he sees is the unfinished page (contradiction), cleanliness 0.42, sleeps at the desk. He is the convicted man's son and cannot finish the family's story because finishing means writing the verdict (web II.1); Cal's reel holds the chapter; Sunday noon he brings two coffees to Noel's door; Saturday nights he holds the Harukiya between songs. Proposed backstory: the rejected endings are all the same chapter. Build state: the main room has the draft, references, cold coffee, radio and a plain bookshelf; the alcove has bed, nightstand, wardrobe. The desk exists only as a dining table; the sightline is not built.

What makes it Jonah Price's is ring stains on every horizontal surface, a wastebasket by the icebox full of paper, cold coffee in three cups, a bread knife in the butter. Three cold coffees, a wastebasket by the icebox full of paper, a bread knife in the butter; the greasy enamel recipe on this range. Light is the kitchen linear or flush dome and the window; the Vantry point on the ceiling listens to the kettle.

areas.title: Jonah Price's bathroom
areas.location: Private bathroom off the unit's private hall
areas.narrative: Every V2 bathroom is a windowless 1928 reopening room on one of the four roof ventilators: a painted gravity register, a cast-iron tub or shower receptor, a pedestal basin, a mirror medicine cabinet and a flush dome. What makes this one Jonah Price's is a single adult's ordinary use: one of everything, a second towel that is really a floorcloth. Off the vestibule: a week's beard in the basin, ink on the towel. The room should pass the Shenmue test at the basin: evidence of construction (the register and its painted-over screws), attachment (the cabinet's two fixings), use (the wiping arc on the mirror), age (crazed enamel, a hairline in the tile), maintenance (a replacement chain on the plug) and consequence (a water line on the floor where the curtain leaks).
